utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Good morning, ladies and gentlemen. Can we have the appearances first.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: If your Honours please, my name is Niemann and I appear with my colleagues Ms. McHenry, Mr. Turone, Mr. Khan and Ms. Van Dusschoten for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Can we have the appearances for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning your Honours, I am Edina Residovic, Defence counsel for Mr. Zejnil Delalic. Defending Mr. Delalic with me is my colleague, Eugene O'Sullivan, professor from Canada.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: Good morning your Honours, my name is Zeljko Olujic, I am Defence counsel of Mr. Zdravko Mucic together with my colleague Mr. Michael Greaves, attorney from the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland. Before I sit down, may I ask the court's indulgence to make an observation, that as Defence counsel for Mr. Zdravko Mucic I had asked the office of the Prosecution to enable a contact or interview with the witness who was not under protection yesterday, to be notified via the office of the Prosecution today that this witness is requesting protection and is also refusing to have any contact with the Defence, not with the Defence of all the defendants, but specifically with me, the Defence counsel of Mr. Zdravko Mucic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARABDIC
utterances.text: Good morning, your Honour. I am Salih Karabdic, attorney from Sarajevo, together with Mr. Thomas Moran, attorney from Houston, I am defending Mr. Hazim Delic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Good morning your Honours, I am John Ackerman. I appear here today with my co-counsel Cynthia McMurray and we appear on behalf of Mr. Esad Landzo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Mr. Niemann, do you know anything about Mr. Olujic's complaint?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour, I will ask Ms. McHenry to address the court on this matter. This witness will be taken by her and in fact there is a motion being filed this morning in relation to that witness which she can refer to as well, your Honour. I will ask Ms. McHenry to deal with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Good morning, your Honours. With respect to what Olujic has said, he is correct in his observations, although I do not believe there is anything improper about either of them. It is the case that this witness, the Prosecution had not requested protective measures for the witness who is scheduled next, and yesterday afternoon, late yesterday afternoon, the witness indicated that he did wish certain protective measures. The Prosecution believes his fears and concerns are warranted and filed -- we advised Defence counsel at the conclusion of court that we would be making a request for protective measures which was filed first thing this morning, so Mr. Olujic is correct that this witness had not previously asked for protective measures and has done so. It is an entirely separate matter that I did receive, through someone from the Office of the Prosecutor, Mr. Olujic's request and subsequently another request from Defence counsel. The request of Defence counsel to interview this witness was conveyed to the witness, the Prosecution did not take a position on it, and the witness decided that he did not wish to speak to Defence counsel. I believe that has happened before on many occasions and I believe it is entirely the witness's own decision, so other than to say Mr. Olujic has correctly stated what happened, that is correct, I do not believe there is anything wrong with anything that happened. If I would, I would just also use this opportunity to inform your Honours that there is this motion for protective measures for the upcoming witness. Obviously the Prosecution apologises for the fact it was not filed beforehand, but we only found out about it yesterday afternoon and there are some extenuating circumstances, this witness has travelled a very long time and it was hard, there were some difficulties beforehand which may explain why the request was not made sooner. But in any event, the request has been made, Defence counsel has been given copies of the motion and we are happy to argue it, whenever your Honours prefer. The only thing I would request is that whenever it is argued, either now, in closed session or at a break, or whenever your Honours wish, it at least be in time enough so that I can talk with the witness and tell him what the court's decision is and then to the extent that the protective measures are granted, explain to him a little bit about how they work. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Frankly, I am not too familiar with why Mr. Olujic thinks anybody can compel a person to speak to him. I suppose if the Prosecution witness declines to talk to a Defence counsel, I do not know what are our procedural rules to compel him to do so. I take it that is part of the hazards of meeting a Defence or any witness whatsoever who does not want to co-operate with you. When he comes to give his evidence, you can get whatever you want to get out of him, but since the Prosecution itself is not responsible for his refusal, there is nothing the Trial Chamber can do about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: If I may, your Honours, I quite understand what you are saying, your Honour, but what I am surprised by, as Defence counsel for Mr. Mucic, is that at the point in time when I requested an interview, that was the moment when the witness asked for application. Up to that moment, he did not ask for protection and this provoked a surprise on my part. Far from it for me to believe that the Prosecution or anyone can compel a witness to talk to me, but I felt it my duty to draw the attention of the court to this fact, because this is a coincidence which, to put it mildly, causes suspicion as regards the request of the witness for protective measures but, of course, we will have occasion to hear him in the examination-in-chief and cross-examination and draw our own conclusions. Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, when will it please the court to hear this motion because unlike other motions, I intend to oppose this request for protection for the simple reason that the Prosecutor's evidence shows that this man is a rapist and a war criminal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We will soon know when we will take the application. This morning, we will go through from now until 1.00 pm. We do not have to break, so we will be able to take all the things we want to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Ms. McHenry, I think I can guess what this witness says. His name has already come in the transcript in the evidence of one or two witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Your Honour, once again, first of all let me say that I would like any discussion about the motion for protective orders to be held in private session, including any accusations that Defence counsel wish to make. Let me also state that as is normally the case, this witness is not asking -- the witness's protective measures, what he is requesting, is not the fact that he was at the camp and, indeed, not even the fact that he worked at the camp, it is the fact that he is a witness and so his identity as a witness is what he seeks protection for, his face.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: I am just drawing your attention to the fact that his name has already come in the transcript playing a certain role. I have a very good guess who that witness is.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: That is correct, your Honour and I believe it is the case with almost all the protected witnesses we have had that there has been some discussion in open testimony about their being at Celebici. As long as I have the floor, let me, if I may, respond to Mr. Olujic. The request for protective measures by the witness was made previous to him being informed of any request by the Defence counsel, so although it is the case that Defence counsel may have been told about them at the same time, they are in fact unrelated and the request for protective measures occurred first. Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I think let us invite the witness, Mr. Panzer.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I may also just ask for some assistance from the technical people, because Mr. Turone's earphones are not working. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: In fact, your Honour, I think the earphones here are not working properly either. There seems to be some technical fault.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I think we might be able to take argument on this motion in the afternoon when we come back.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Thank you very much, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Please swear the interpreter. THE INTERPRETER (sworn) WOLFGANG PANZER (resworn)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You are still under cross-examination. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning, Mr. Panzer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Officer Panzer, I would like to talk a little about 18th March 1996, when you said you returned to police headquarters and you were there from 5.00 in the afternoon until 1.30 in the morning on March 19th; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: When you arrived at police headquarters that afternoon you went directly to room 331?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Yesterday you told us that you put the allegedly seized items from Taubergasse 15, Door 10, Door 14, as well as those from INDA-Bau, in a cabinet in room 331?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is partly right. With regard to the seized items from Taubergasse 15, Door 10 and Door 14, I brought them to the police station and Mr. Navrat brought in the items seized at INDA-Bau.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: I understood you yesterday to say that you put them, all those items, in a cabinet in room 331.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: At what time did you do that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I really cannot remember exactly what time it was, but about 5.00 pm.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Yesterday you said, and I am quoting you: "Late in the evening on 18th March I marked the allegedly seized videos from Door 10." Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right, the items seized at Mr. Mucic's apartment, I do not know exactly what time it was, but they were labelled by me that evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: You are saying everything from Door 10 was labelled by you on the evening of the 18th; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Can you help me with this, yesterday you said it was late in the evening. Would that about 10.00, 11.00, midnight, somewhere around there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With regard to the labelling of the items seized at Taubergasse 15, Door 10; in other words at Mr. Mucic's apartment, that was done by me some time between 5.00 pm and at the latest 8.00 pm.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Can you help us out a little bit more? Was it closer to 8.00 perhaps?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would say it was closer to 8.00, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: From the time you put these items in the cabinet until you marked these items, did they remain the whole time in the cabinet?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they stayed in the cabinet the whole time.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: From 5.00 when you put them there until you took them out to mark them they stayed in the cabinet?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All of the seized items once they were handed over were put in the cabinet and all of the items from the same locality were placed on the same shelf. Now perhaps Mr. Bycek, Mr. Moerbaur and myself in the meantime took something out, had a look at it and put it back in, but they were always in there -- put it this way, I cannot really say that there were in there under lock and key at absolutely all times.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: When you were finished marking the videos and the items from Door 10, you put them back in the cabinet?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I put them back in the box and back in the cabinet, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: They were not removed after that from the cabinet?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot say precisely, perhaps someone wanted to have a look at something, but that would be only one of the individuals present at the search, Bycek, Borlak, Moerbaur, myself, I cannot really say precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: The other items that are in the cabinet, other than Door 10, they remained in the cabinet from the time you put them there about 5.00 on the 18th until some time the next day; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were in the cabinet. The items were always in the cabinet, to put it that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Yesterday you said this about the people who were in room 331 on 18th March, I will just read it to you to remind you and ask you a couple of questions about it. You said this: "On the 18th in that room, for the most part, until the prisoner was handed over, the lady who was interpreting, Ms. Suppert, Mr. Borlak, Mr. Moerbaur, Mr. Bycek, myself, Mr. Gschwendt, who was the legal advisor from the department, Mr. Navrat, who came in to give me the items, I think Mr. Unger, Mr. Winkelmann were in the next office writing a summary report. As I remember, those were the people." My question is this: those were the only people who entered room 331 from 5.00 pm on 18th March until 1.30 in the morning the next day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those people were there and I think in the course of the evening of the 18th there were also people from the Tribunal who were there with the authority of the examining magistrate, they were allowed to have a look at the items seized. As to who they were, I cannot say, but for that purpose items were also taken out and shown to people from the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Did you remain in room 331 during this whole period, from 5.00 pm to 1.30 in the morning?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not in the office itself, I was in the office most of the time, I was in other rooms, I had to copy some things. I had to take care of some things, I had to get together and discuss certain matters with fellow officers, but most of the time I was in office 331.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Now we have a few more people showing up in room 331 than what we had yesterday. In addition to the police officers, we have five people from the Office of the Prosecutor in that office, do we not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you repeat that question, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Let us go back to who was in room 331 between 5.00 and 1.30 in the morning. There is you, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From 5.00 pm, okay, yes I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: During this period from 5.00 pm until 1.30 in the morning on the 19th. You were there, at one point Winkelmann was there --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The 18th we are talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: The 18th, yes, but 1.30 in the morning on the 19th you left. Your colleague Winkelmann was in and out of that office?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Unger and Winkelmann were there for about 20 minutes, not in 331 itself, in the room next door, and they were writing a corrigendum to the search document. Mr. Navrat was there for a brief time, handed the things over to me. Mr. Gschwendt was there occasionally, he came into our office to have a look what was up. He was in charge of the operation as my supervisor. Then there was the legal advisor who was on duty at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Perhaps I could just do it a little more orderly, if you do not mind. You say Navrat -- I will go through it with you, all right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Navrat was in the room and gave me the items seized from INDA-Bau.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Can you say yes or no? Mr. Gschwendt was there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Gschwendt was there occasionally.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Mr. Bycek was there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Bycek was a member of our team and helped out in preparing the relevant documentation.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: And he was in room 331?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: You said Moerbaur was in room 331?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Moerbaur, yes, certainly. Borlak and Moerbaur conducted the interview with Mr. Mucic. That was later on. I think that started after 7.00 pm.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: You said Mr. Winkelmann was in and out of room 331 at some point?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They came into 331, but Messrs Winkelmann and Unger were in the room next door. They gave me that report and then they left, so they spent at most 15 to 20 minutes on those premises.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Mr. Mucic was in 331?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Mucic was sitting next to the typewriter in room 331.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: You said that Ms Lillian Suppert, the interpreter, was in room 331?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Ms. Suppert came in as well. She had been notified by Mr. Gschwendt in the meantime and when we came in she was already in the room with Mr. Gschwendt, so she came over to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Then there were people from the office of the Prosecution in that room, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know, I do not know what you mean, office of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: The office of the Prosecution of this Tribunal, their representatives were also in room 331.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: People from the Tribunal looked in. As to when that was and how long they were there, I cannot say. They were not in room 331, they were rather in the room next door. As far as I know, Dr Seda, the examining magistrate and the people from Interpol had agreed that they could be present in the course of the questioning and that they could also have a look at the items seized. Then subsequently they were provided with copies of the videotapes and of the seized documents. As to whether that was Monday 18th or not I cannot say, but I myself did make copies on behalf of people from the Tribunal. In fact what I copied were the tapes seized at the apartment of Mr. Mucic, but that was not on the 18th, that was either on the 20th or the 21st, I cannot really say.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: I want to deal right now with just the 18th, all right? Here is my next question. On the 18th, between 5.00 and 1.30 in the morning, you say that the representatives of the Prosecutor's office of this Tribunal were never in room 331; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They did come into that room, but they were staying, as it were, in the room next door. That is where they were located, as it were.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: There were five people in total from the Office of the Prosecutor; is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Maybe I can help you. Do you remember a Mr. Du Toit, a South African legal advisor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know the names, Du Toit, Nicholson, D'Hooge, I remember those names. As to whether all those people were in the room, in the room next door, I cannot really say, I was going about other tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: My question was, do you remember Mr. Du Toit, the South African man who was a legal advisor? Do you remember him being in room 331?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know Mr. Du Toit first hand but I cannot say now whether he was in the room or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Do you remember whether Mr. Abribat the French police officer was in room 331?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I only know that there were people there, but I cannot recall their names.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Maybe I can help you just one last time with Mr. D'Hooge, the Belgian police officer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: D'Hooge, I know him by name and first hand, but I cannot say with certainty whether he was there or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: If I speak his name in German, would that help you -- you recall speaking in German with Mr. D'Hooge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: What time did the representatives of the Office of the Prosecutor arrive that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am afraid I cannot tell you, I cannot tell you when they arrived, when they left. I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: You do not know when they left?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know that either.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: The interview you conducted with Mr. Mucic started about 7.30 or 7.00 you said, is that right, the police interview?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think so, but that should be discernible on the basis of the relevant document there, the record where on the upper right-hand corner the time at which that interview began should be indicated.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: To your recollection it was around 7.00 pm; is that not right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think so. As to the exact time of the interview there is the record there of the interview with Mr. Mucic.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: By the time that interview with Mr. Mucic had begun the representatives of the Office of the Prosecutor had left; is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: The interview with Mr. Mucic took place in room 331, did it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: So is it not correct that the Office of the Prosecutor's representatives were not in 331 at that point, they had left?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Basically, besides the persons directly involved there was no one in the room where the interview took place; that is to say room 331.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: So far we have gone over a list here and I have got about 10 to 12 people in room 331 that evening. Does that sound about right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That could be right.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: If the interpreter might just correct the previous answer, no one remained in the room for any length of time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Now if you look at the person arrested, the interpreter, Borlak, Bycek, myself, then short basis, Unger and Winkelmann then in the meantime, the legal advisor, Magister Famler, then on an off and on basis my supervisor Mr. Gschwendt and a few people from the Tribunal, that would bring you to about the stated number.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Yesterday you told me there was only about seven, so it has changed overnight, has it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You are right.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Is it not correct that in room 331 the representatives of the Office of the Prosecutor were allowed to look at the allegedly seized items from Door 10, Door 14 and INDA-Bau?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: These items were placed on a table, one of the times in room 331.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think they were in the room next door on the table, the seized items I took them out of the cabinet. I and Mr. Moerbaur gave it to them, they had a look at it, then I took it back and put it back in the cabinet.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: This took place in room 331?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not in room 331 but in the room next door. I believe it is number 329.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: An investigator from the Office of the Prosecutor was allowed to examine items, right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I know, all of the people from the Tribunal had a look at these items, or had a brief look at them, shall we say.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: That included the interpreter who was from the Office of the Prosecutor; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know who the interpreter was. I was not aware who the interpreter was. I think it may have been Ms. Pal, but at all events, there had been the authorisation there from the examining magistrate and I acted in a manner consistent with that authorisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: And the people from the Office of the Prosecutor requested that certain documents be photocopied, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is possible. I cannot really say as to whether anything was copied or not. I only know that in the following days a certain amount of material was copied as well as the four videotapes and that they were handed over to the people from the Tribunal, but as I said, always with the accord of the examining magistrate.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: So, to your knowledge nothing was photocopied on the 18th between 5.00 pm and 1.30 in the morning on the next day; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot say. I do not remember whether on the 18th there had already been photocopies made. I simply cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: And the representatives of the Tribunal also asked to view videos, is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know that I had a look at a video with Mr. Du Toit, that I remember, but was that on the 18th? I really cannot say.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: You see what you have told us here is a little bit different to what your colleague Moerbaur told us when he came to testify. Moerbaur said that these items were spread out on a table in room 331 and the Office of the Prosecutor was allowed to look at them. What do you say to that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Moerbaur, at the point in time when I was elsewhere, was looking at things with people from the Tribunal in 331.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Both Mr. Moerbaur and Mr. D'Hooge who testified here said that this took place between approximately 5.00 and 7.30 on the evening of 18th March 1996. What do you say to that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not say anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: So it is not correct, is it, to say that the allegedly seized items remained for the most part in the cabinet in room 331, as you told us earlier.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The items were locked up in the cabinet most or all of the time. Of course, it does not apply to the time during which the items were taken out and looked at either by ourselves or the people from the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Mr. Moerbaur says he photocopied some documents and handed over come copies and, in fact, some originals that were taken away by the Office of the Prosecutor. Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said earlier on that I cannot remember that on 18th March there were copies made of documents. With regard to what Mr. Moerbaur said, I cannot comment on that therefore.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Help me understand something. Mr. Mucic was arrested under an Austrian arrest warrant, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The arrest warrant was issued by an Austrian court.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: And the alleged search and seizures, all of them on the 18th, were carried out pursuant to two Austrian search warrants; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The warrants, arrest and search warrants, were issued by an Austrian court and were executed in compliance with Austrian law.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: So Mr. Mucic was the prisoner of the Austrian authorities on the 18th; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: When you conducted a police interview with him in which you participated, you were required to do so under Austrian law, were you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: And after the interview you were required to take Mr. Mucic to jail, which you did.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is not right. Mr. Mucic was brought to the police jail only after the questioning of the interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: That is correct. That was required under Austrian law.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right. An arrested person has to be questioned forthwith in connection with a case. That is in the relevant legislation. If there is no basis then the examining magistrate has to be informed and the person can be released. As things turned out differently, Mr. Mucic was handed over to the police jail at 1.30 on the morning of the 19th.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Is it also correct that under Austrian law, persons not involved in operations concerning Mr. Mucic could not have access to him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Mucic was informed of his rights at the scene at the moment of arrest, in the apartment by his daughter and then he was informed of his rights when we arrived at office 331, he was informed by Ms. Suppert. There is the information sheet for arrested persons that at the time was in German, but Ms. Suppert translated that word for word and the rights of an arrested person are spelled out there. There it says that he can notify a person of his confidence, he can notify a counsel et cetera, and Mr. Mucic did not make use of that possibility and that is something that is confirmed in the custody report where you can see his signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: I will repeat my question. Please listen to it and please answer it. Under Austrian law, Mr. Mucic, because he was your prisoner, could not be contacted the by people who were not authorised to do so; is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Mucic at any point of time, if he had chosen to do, could have notified a person of his confidence or a lawyer, at any point in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: That is provided for in the law.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: If there is no provision in the law for contact with Mr. Mucic, no other person could contact him; is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Mr. Mucic at this point, on the 18th, was not the prisoner of the authorities of this Tribunal, was he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Mucic on the 18th was a prisoner of the Vienna police department.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: What is true about Mr. Mucic, contact with him by unauthorised people, is also true for the allegedly seized items; that is no one without legal authorisation could have contact with those allegedly seized items; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I object to that, your Honour. The basis of the objection, your Honour, is that the witness has answered this question a number of times in saying that the access by the Office of the Prosecutor to the documents was authorised by Dr Seda. In my submission the question has been asked and answered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I am satisfied with the objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: I will ask this question then. Mr. Panzer, did you tell the representatives of the Office of the Prosecutor that Dr Seda had given his consent for them to examine these allegedly seized items?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On Monday 18th March, in the morning there had been a meeting at Interpol's premises, and there were present there the people from the Tribunal, the people from Interpol, my superior, Mr. Gschwendt and the district court, and as far as I was aware on the basis of what Mr. Gschwendt told me, it had been agreed that representatives of the Tribunal could be present at the questioning and could look at the seized items. At some point in time the question cropped up about videotapes. That matter, however, was not settled. In response to your question, all I can say is that Dr Seda gave his consent. I know that, Mr. Gschwendt told me in the course of several conversations, and what you have to bear in mind is that at the time we were in a certain legal vacuum, as it were. There was not yet the Federal Law about co-operation with international tribunals. That legal basis was adopted by -- at the time it was in the Parliament before a specialised committee. That legal basis, that is to say the law for co-operation with the International Tribunal, was not adopted until 1st June 1996; that is to say some time after the arrest of Mr. Mucic. So every step that was taken, every detail, was discussed either by myself or by Mr. Gschwendt with the examining magistrate.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: You say that Dr Seda gave approval, is this approval in writing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: You have never seen a document to this effect, have you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not a document relevant to this, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: A few minutes ago I asked you a very specific question, I would like you to answer it now. Please listen to it, it is a simple yes or no question, I think. Did you tell the representatives of the Office of the Prosecutor of this Tribunal that Dr Seda had agreed to allow them to look at, handle and photocopy documents on 18th March?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Do you know whether any of your colleagues told them that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can only remember that this matter had been settled by Mr. Gschwendt and Mr. Gschwendt told me that these people could do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: You see the problem I am having, sir, is that Bart D'Hooge was a witness here, you have already said he was in Vienna that night, and he had this to say at pages 4001 and 4002 of the transcript. He said: "The police could not contact Dr Seda for authorisation. It was after working hours and probably Dr Seda was not in his office." That is what Mr. D'Hooge said happened that night. I put it to you there was never any authorisation from Dr Seda on 18th March to examine documents; is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot judge that. My superior, Mr. Gschwendt, informed me that in the course of a discussion on Monday morning that possibility had been discussed and that the authorisation had been granted and that is all I am saying about the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: It comes down to your word against D'Hooge's, does it not, if there are no documents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Okay. Let us talk a little bit about Taubergasse 15, Door 10, where Mr. Mucic was brought after his arrest. He did not leave Door 10 until he was brought back to police headquarters around 4.30; is that right? He remained at apartment 10 the whole time?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: May the interpreter ask that the question be repeated?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Yes. From the time he was arrested and brought to Door 10, Mr. Mucic did not leave that apartment until he was brought back to headquarters.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: During that time his daughter Sanda was with him in the apartment; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The daughter was present in the apartment at times.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: With the assistance of the usher I would like to show -- I would ask that Prosecution Exhibit 151 be shown to the witness. You are looking at the Niederschrift for Door 10; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: You see that the date typed in at the top of the page and the date written in at the bottom of the page are incorrect?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 19/3/96, that is written by the typewriter, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Down below by hand it says 19th March and those dates are wrong because you say this search took place on the 18th; is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The arrest and the house search took place on the 18th March 1996. The explanation for the wrong date --

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Are the dates wrong or not? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On this document the dates are wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: And the bottom line where the time should be filled in, nothing is indicated; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right, there is nothing there.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: You signed this document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I signed the document, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: And you read it before you signed it; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Under Austrian law is there not a report, a Bericht of this house search which is prepared immediately after that document as required by law?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, the report, yes, that comes after.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: And in the case of Door 10, no such document was ever prepared, was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The report was produced in connection with the arrest warrant.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: But there is no -- in the police file, there is no such Bericht, house search; none was prepared; is that not right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have the report here, I can show it to the counsel if he so wishes.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: The typed in parts of this Niederschrift, you told us, were prepared before the search of Door 10 by your colleague Bycek; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct. As we have already said on a number of occasions the operation was supposed to be carried out on the 19th at 6.00 am.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Could you look at the second page where the confiscated are there? They are typed in, are they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can see.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: So that was typed in before the search?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This inventory of the seized items was produced by Mr. Bycek in the office after the operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: And Mr. Mucic also signed this document in the office, not on the premises; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the apartment, as far as I remember, he signed the search warrant and the arrest warrant and the paper 150 was signed by him at police headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: And this paper 150, the Niederschrift, is the only document that is prepared on the spot to show what has been seized, and the witness confirms that; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In his apartment, Door 10. We only have here who was in his apartment, who took part in the search at apartment 10. The rest was done by Mr. Bycek at headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: I would like to talk a bit about INDA-Bau. The search there took place on 18th March; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Could I ask that the witness be shown D57/1, please? (Handed). This is the report you prepared on April 22nd 1996; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: I move to have this document admitted, your Honour, admitted into evidence. It is D57/1, I move to have it admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honour, might I have a look at the document, please? We seem to have some trouble locating our copy. May I see the witness's copy? (Handed). I have no objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Sir, this is the report that you prepared in connection with the alleged search at INDA-Bau; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is an inventory of seized items. That is the report, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: In this report you make reference to twelve files.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: You note that there are 54 cassettes, video cassettes; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: I ask that the witness be shown Prosecution Exhibit 165 and 165A. Do you recognise that as the Niederschrift prepared in connection with INDA-Bau?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is the Niederschrift, paper 150, that Mr. Navrat filled in and gave to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: And the date at the top is incorrect; March 19th is the wrong date, is it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 19th March is on the Niederschrift and it is wrong, that is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: At the bottom where the date should go there is a blank; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was not filled in.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: And the time is not indicated at the bottom either?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right too.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: And the line where the names of the police officers should go at the top, all we have is numbers; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct. It is a possibility in Austria that you write in your service number, so that you can take precautions against any claims that might be made later on. I think the number is Mr. Navrat, 1021 and the others are for people from the 16th District.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: We are looking at this document, we have no idea who these people are, to whom the numbers refer; is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is not necessary. It is enough that you put the service number in.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: I did not ask if it was necessary. I said there is no way of knowing who these people are, is that not correct, from looking at this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I object to that your Honour. That is misrepresentation of the position.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: I will ask the witness this: is it possible to make any connection between the numbers and the police officers who may have conducted the search by looking at this document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Actually, if I understand what the witness is saying, he is saying you can identify them by their service numbers. This is what he is saying. Although their names are not there, their service number is there.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Going back to your report, the previous document we looked at, you said that there were 54 videos coming from INDA-Bau; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: In this Niederschrift it says there are 51; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is what it says, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Can I ask that the witness be shown Exhibit D56/1? (Handed). Sir, you are looking at a report dated March 18th 1996 prepared by Navrat. Have you seen this before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is the report on the house search that Mr. Navrat carried out in Koppstrasse 14 in the 16th District on 18th March. I know this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: In this report it says there are 51 videos.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, that is what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: You claim that you marked these videos or these videos were marked for the first time by you on 19th March; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was on the 19th or the 20th that I marked the videos, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: In fact everything coming from INDA-Bau was unmarked until you marked on the 19th or 20th; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: And the first indication of the change in number of videos is 22nd April, in your report.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: With the assistance of the usher I would like to have a document shown to the witness. I have copies for your Honours and the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document is marked D64/1.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Sir, you are looking at a report prepared by you on April 22nd 1996; is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: I move to have this document admitted into evidence, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No objections, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: It is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: This is a report you prepared in connection with Taubergasse 15, Door 14; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: In this report you note that there are 28 video cassettes, right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: You prepared this document in part based on the Niederschrift which was prepared by Unger and Winkelmann; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct. It is just an inventory, this document, a list of the things that were listed, that we made an inventory of. Nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: With the help of the usher I have another document to show the witness, please. There you have a copy of the Niederschrift prepared by Winkelmann and Unger prepared in connection with Door 14; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I know this Niederschrift as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: This is document 65 --

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: At this time I move to have this document admitted into evidence, your Honour. Is the document so admitted, your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Thank you. The search of Door 14 took place on 18th March, right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On 18th March, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: So the typed in date of 19th March at the top and the handwritten date of 19th March at the bottom are both wrong, are they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: On the second page the record indicates that Sanda Mucic was the witness to this alleged search and seizure; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: And yesterday we established by looking at documents that she was only 16 years old; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: According to what the birth date says, yes, she was 16.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: At Taubergasse 15 that day the brother of Zejnil Delalic, Dzemal Delalic, was present, was he not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Yesterday you told us that the sister-in-law of Zejnil Delalic, Harisa was also present that day at Taubergasse 15?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, during the afternoon she was at Taubergasse 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Sir, you are familiar with Article 142, paragraph 2 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, are you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Which says that if the owner of the premises is not available --

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Object, your Honour. Criminal procedure of what country: China, Japan, Austria?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Pardon me, your Honour, I will rephrase that question. The code of procedure of Austria, the one under which you operate. Article 142(2) says that if the owner of the premises is not present then an adult member of his family shall be present or a fellow lodger, neighbour, if members of the family are not there. Those are the people who must witness a search; is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know this paragraph, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: In all cases must be an adult; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The paragraph stipulates that it has to be an adult, that is right, adult member of the family.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Going back to your report, there you list 28 videos and in the Niederschrift there are 30 videos; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: We have heard from you, and in fact every other Viennese police officer who has testified here, that the items seized from Taubergasse 15 and the items seized at INDA-Bau were brought back in containers that were not sealed. Under the Austrian code of criminal procedure, Article 145, paragraph 3 states the following: "The documents which are to be used in judicial proceedings and which cannot be promptly recorded shall be put in an envelope and sealed with an official seal. The person whose documents are being searched shall be allowed, if that person is present during the search, to put his own seal on the envelope. If the seal should be broken the person whose documents were searched shall be invited to attend. In the event that the person receives the summons and fail to appear, or if the summons could not be served on that person on the grounds of his absence, the seal shall nevertheless be broken." Are you familiar with this provision?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: This article deals with sealing seized items on the spot to preserve evidence, does it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is what it says in this paragraph, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: You are familiar with this paragraph, you said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I know the paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Police officers in your division who carry out searches and are made aware of this provision through their training and experience, are they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they also know these paragraphs.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Could I ask that the witness be shown several documents, have them placed in front of him. D64/1, D65/1 and Prosecution Exhibit 104. (Handed).

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, might I know what is being placed before the witness. I know it was D64/1, but were there other documents as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: D64/1, D65/1 and Prosecution Exhibit 104. Officer Panzer, could I ask you to look first at the Niederschrift for Door 14, which is one of the two documents on your left. Do you have that document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. You mean the Niederschrift?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Yes, which has been marked as D65/1.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS

utterances.text: If you look at this document, there you see no reference to a green folder at all, do you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: The document you are looking at is the second document or the one that is prepared after the Niederschrift, is that right, in the succession of documents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Counsel, what do you mean by second document? You mean the report of 22nd April 1996?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I think that is the document "Vienna police main office, Division 1".

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
